newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli jets hit Hizbollah in northeast Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli jets hit Hizbollah in northeast Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli jets hit Hizbollah guerrilla targets deep in northeast Lebanon near the Syrian border on Thursday, in apparent retaliation for the killing of an Israeli soldier by the guerrillas, security sources said.

Hizbollah (Party of God) swiftly said after the raid that it would step up its attacks in south Lebanon where Israeli troops occupy a 15 km (nine miles) deep zone to ward off guerrilla attacks on northern Israel.

The sources said the air raid targeted an empty scouts camp for the pro-Iranian guerrilla faction on the banks of the Assi River in the remote Hermel region, 10 km (six miles) west of the border with Syria.

The raid caused damage but no casualties, according to Hizbollah officials at the site, some 55 km (33 miles) north of the city of Baalbek, the main bastion of the fundamentalist group in eastern Lebanon's Bekaa Valley.
A Reuters reporter saw Red Cross ambulances enter the camp and leave empty. Witnesses said four jets fired four rockets into the camp, destroying five of its 16 brick-and-zinc rooms.

The air raid was the 24th against Lebanon this year. Almost one year ago Israel launched a 17-day military bombardment of southern Lebanon in an attempt to drive out Hizbollah guerrillas. The Israeli operation killed more than 200 people, most of them Lebanese civilians.

The air attack on Thursday followed the killing of one Israeli soldier and the wounding of three others in a Hizbollah guerrilla raid on Wednesday against an Israeli patrol in the israeli-occupied border zone in south Lebanon.
In Israel, the army on Thursday confirmed one soldier was killed and three wounded, two of them seriously, in the raid.
Wednesday's casualties raised to six the number of Israeli soldiers killed in south Lebanon this year. Last year, 27 Israelis were killed in Lebanon.

Hours after the air raid, Hizbollah's top official in the Bekaa Valley, Mohammad Yaghi, vowed that Hizbollah would step up its military operations against Israeli forces and would be in an "open war (with Israel) to defeat its criminal designs".

The latest Israel-Hizbollah violence came after Israel broke ground on Tuesday for the building of homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem in a step that drew fire from some European countries, Arab states and anti-Israeli Islamist and Palestinian guerrilla groups.

Hizbollah (Party of God) is leading a guerrilla war to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 SLA militiamen from the zone in south Lebanon set up by Israel to stop cross-frontier guerrilla raids on northern Israel.
